searchText: rollups are *not* part of ethereum in the way parachains are in dot Is the plan still to start sharded eth with 64 shards, with an architecture that'll support 1024 shards? This could be the misconception Mr.Dav has. A L2 with state sync is not theoretically less secure than Ethereum. It could have the same amount of non-staking validators as ETH, relative to network size. Currently rollups are smaller than mainnet, but that could change. Such validators only need the L1 state and L2 state, not L1 historical calldata. Is there a limit to the number of shards? If most of the L2 layers, access the L1 layer at the same time, will it cause congestion and spike the GAS cost? Will the unchanged L1 layer drag down ETH in the future? ETH is known as a dirt-cheap chain, and its GAS fees are too high these days. A rollup with some other state distribution system would need to actually design and build this state distribution system. I don't think anyone has actually done that.
